text.en: A shoemaker wants wheat, but the farmer wants cloth. Barter fails without a double coincidence of wants. Money solves this, and credit helps people start businesses.

In barter, goods are exchanged directly and it needs a double coincidence of wants. Money removes this trouble because it is accepted as a medium of exchange.
Modern forms of money are currency, paper notes and coins, and deposits with banks. In India the Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes.
People keep money in bank accounts, which are demand deposits. Cheques allow payments without cash.
Banks keep a part of deposits as cash and lend the rest. They earn interest on loans, which is more than they pay on deposits.
Credit or loan is an agreement where the lender supplies money and expects repayment. Terms of credit include interest rate, collateral, documentation and mode of repayment.
Formal sources of credit are banks and cooperatives, supervised by the RBI. Informal sources are moneylenders and traders who often charge high interest.
Self Help Groups pool small savings of 15 to 20 members, mostly women, and lend among themselves, which gives credit without collateral.
Debt trap occurs when a borrower cannot repay and falls deeper into debt. So cheap credit from formal sources is important.

problem.en: A loan of Rs 10,000 at 10 per cent yearly simple interest. What interest after one year?

prompt.en: Why is formal credit better for poor households?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking moneylenders always charge the same

points.en: Money solves barter's double coincidence of wants.
Formal credit is cheaper than informal credit.
SHGs help the poor with small loans.
